title: Crumpets
subtitle: Yeasted griddle cakes with a spongy, hole-filled texture
excerpt: Homemade crumpets with a deep honeycomb of holes that soak up butter and hold it until the last bite. Far better than shop-bought, and easier to make than most people expect.

recipe.sourceNotes: Crumpets are a British yeasted griddle cake with a characteristic spongy texture and the deep honeycomb of holes on the top surface that allow butter to pool and soak in. They are distinct from English muffins (which are also yeasted but not holey and are baked in the oven after toasting) and from pikelets (a thinner, holey griddle cake made from the same batter but without rings to confine it). Crumpets are cooked in metal rings on a griddle: the batter is liquid enough to pour and the rings prevent it spreading. The holes are formed by carbon dioxide bubbles from the yeast and bicarbonate of soda rising through the liquid batter and breaking on the surface. A good crumpet has holes that go deep enough to hold a generous amount of butter. Crumpets originated in the Midlands of England and are now eaten throughout the United Kingdom, traditionally for breakfast or afternoon tea.

recipeTools.notes: A flat griddle or heavy frying pan. Four 9 cm metal crumpet rings or pastry cutters.

content.text: The batter should be slightly thicker than single cream but still pourable. The holes form as the crumpet cooks: do not interfere until the top surface has dried and set, which takes about 8 minutes. If the holes fill in or the surface looks glassy rather than spongy, the heat may be too low. If the bottom burns before the top sets, the heat is too high. Medium-low is the correct temperature for crumpets. Grease the rings between each batch to prevent sticking.

items.preparation: for greasing the rings and pan

content.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a bowl. Add the warm milk and 200 ml of warm water. Whisk to a smooth, pourable batter. Cover and leave in a warm place for 45 minutes to 1 hour until the batter is bubbly and has risen slightly. Stir in the bicarbonate of soda dissolved in 1 tablespoon of warm water.

Heat a flat griddle or heavy frying pan over medium-low heat. Grease the pan and the inside of the crumpet rings with oil. Place the rings in the pan. Pour a ladleful of batter into each ring to about 1 cm deep.

Cook for 8 to 10 minutes without moving until the top surface is covered with bubbles and has set and dried. Lift off the rings. If the top is still very wet, leave for another minute. The crumpets do not need to be flipped but can be briefly toasted on the top for 1 minute if preferred. Serve immediately with butter, or allow to cool and toast before buttering.
